channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Flávio promete a Trump Pix, Mercosul, soberania, terras raras e honra
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL candidate, promises in a letter to Donald Trump to align Brazil’s policies with U.S. interests, including conditionally imposing tariffs based on election outcomes (favorable if he wins, unfavorable if Lula wins), dissolving Mercosul to benefit the U.S., granting rare earth minerals to the U.S., and using PIX as an economic alignment tool. His stance reflects a vision of strategic Brazilian subordination to the U.S., prioritizing personal and partisan gains over national sovereignty.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro quer premiar Trump pelo ataque ao Pix
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro proposes rewarding Donald Trump for attacking Pix, claiming the Brazilian payment system harms foreign companies like Visa and Mastercard. The statement emerges amid rising trade tensions between the U.S. and Brazil, with Washington accusing Pix of unfair competition practices. The federal deputy argues Brazil should compensate Trump for alleged damages to American corporations.

item.title: Crusoé: Atropelada
item.description: Lula’s government entered its third year politically weakened, with 2025 beginning with the dollar at record levels due to the botched announcement of fiscal adjustment by Fernando Haddad. In an attempt to recover and remain politically viable for this year’s election, the president abandoned any pretense of fiscal responsibility, deepening the crisis of confidence.

item.title: Gratuidade do Farmácia Popular é maior acerto de Lula, diz AtlasIntel
item.description: The free provision of medicines through the Farmácia Popular program was rated as the main success of Lula's government by 84% of respondents in the June 2026 AtlasIntel/Bloomberg survey, followed by income tax exemption for earnings under R$ 5,000 (80%). The fiscal arcabouço and reversal of privatizations were the worst-rated policies, seen as errors by 46% and 48% respectively. Lula holds the highest positive image among tested leaders at 46%, while Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has the worst, with 90% negative perception.

item.title: Para 50%, novos casos de corrupção de Lula são “muito prováveis”
item.description: According to the Latam Pulse survey from June, released by AtlasIntel/Bloomberg, 50% of Brazilians consider it 'very likely' that new corruption cases involving President Lula will emerge during the remainder of his third term. An additional 34% view this scenario as probable to some extent, while only 10% and 7% deem it 'unlikely' or 'very unlikely', respectively. The survey, with a 1 percentage point margin of error and 95% confidence level, also finds that a coup d'état and Lula's removal from office are seen as unlikely by most respondents.

item.title: Para 52%, economia do Brasil está “ruim”
item.description: The June 2026 Latam Pulse survey by AtlasIntel/Bloomberg shows that 52% of Brazilian voters view the country's economic situation as 'bad', while 36% rate it as 'good' and 13% as 'normal'. Despite current pessimism, 48% expect economic improvement in the next six months, compared to 39% anticipating deterioration and 13% foreseeing no change. The poll surveyed 4,999 people nationwide from June 26–30, with a 1 percentage point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Argentina x Cabo Verde na Copa: onde assistir, horário e escalações
item.description: Argentina and Cape Verde face off on Friday, July 3, at 7:00 p.m. Brasília time, in Miami, in the Round of 16 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Argentina, the defending champions and undefeated in Group J, are expected to start Lionel Messi. Cape Verde, making its World Cup debut, advanced to the knockout stage unbeaten with three draws and made history as the least populous nation to reach a World Cup knockout round.

item.title: Análise: Flávio Bolsonaro tem ataque de 'sincericídio' e negocia com os EUA tarifaço para depois das eleições
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro urged U.S. authorities to delay a potential tariff on Brazilian goods until after the 2026 elections, a move described as a 'political slip of the tongue' because it reveals his priority is avoiding electoral damage, not resolving the trade dispute. Lula condemned the request, accusing the Bolsonaro family of acting against national interests and potentially inviting new U.S. tariffs to undermine his re-election bid. Flávio’s strategy weakens his bargaining power by publicly disclosing his intent to delay the measure.

item.title: PT explora críticas de aliado de Flávio Bolsonaro sobre voto feminino
item.description: The PT published a video linking Flávio Bolsonaro to influencer Paulo Figueiredo, who claimed women 'vote poorly,' especially single women, and criticized Michelle Bolsonaro. The video implies that Flávio’s allies could influence his presidential decisions. Flávio publicly rejected Figueiredo’s remarks, stating he is not part of his campaign, though Figueiredo said he remains supportive.

item.title: Entre trancos e barrancos
item.description: The 2026 presidential campaign between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro is characterized by weak debates and mutual blame-shifting, with few merits highlighted and an emphasis on opponents' mistakes. Lula leans on his past record and blames external forces like the market and agribusiness for Brazil's problems, while Flávio relies on his father's political legacy and struggles with internal divisions within bolsonarism. Both lack a new agenda, reducing the race to who makes fewer errors amid political fatigue and reliance on legacy.

item.title: Ambos negam, mas Paulo Figueiredo dita o que Flavio Bolsonaro fala
item.description: Paulo Figueiredo is shaping Flávio Bolsonaro’s statements, despite both denying any direction. The conflict escalated after a video by former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro criticized the pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, sparking accusations of gender-based political violence, as reported by Thais Bilenky in A Hora on UOL.

item.title: O que a overdose de propaganda oficial revela sobre Lula e o PT
item.description: The Lula government allocated a record R$ 520 million for official propaganda in the first half of 2026, during an election year, according to Folha de S.Paulo. Actress Luana Piovani condemned the spending as 'a slap in the face of Brazilians,' questioning the prioritization of funds amid ongoing social challenges.

item.title: Pesquisas internas detectam desgaste de Flávio junto a público feminino
item.description: Internal polls show growing wear of Flávio Bolsonaro among female voters, particularly following his public feud with stepmother Michelle Bolsonaro and the misogynistic statement by his ally Paulo Figueiredo. The gap between the candidate and women voters has widened this week, according to daily voter monitoring conducted for politicians and financial market agents.

item.title: Ministro de Lula contraria Banco Mundial ao propor imposto do pecado ‘light’
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan opposed a World Bank study by advocating for maintaining current tax levels on harmful products (alcohol, tobacco, betting) when the selective tax begins in 2027, aiming to avoid controversial debates. The Lula government fears electoral backlash from tax increases ahead of the 2026 elections, though the Ministry states that final rates depend on congressional approval.

item.title: Lula diz que eleitor precisa pensar na família ao escolher candidato
item.description: Lula da Silva stated that voters must consider their family and future when choosing the next president, urging them to research candidates' biographies to avoid electing someone who would harm the country, likening it to putting a 'fox in the henhouse'. He emphasized evaluating which candidate delivered more in essential areas and who is most respected internationally, and asked Governor Elmano de Freitas to keep the campaign at a high level.

item.title: Governo Lula leva aos EUA "mapa" de compensações para evitar tarifaço
item.description: The Lula government presented U.S. officials with a 'roadmap' offering compensatory measures in areas such as digital trade, intellectual property, ethanol, and illegal deforestation to avoid a proposed 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods. The proposal, shared during negotiations in Washington, aims to show that Brazilian policies do not distort U.S. trade, while keeping the Pix payment system off the negotiating table. Machinery, health equipment, and information technology are three sectors that could be discussed for mutual tariff reductions.

item.title: Após crise com Michelle, Flávio defenderá indicação de mulheres ao STF
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a 2026 presidential hopeful, plans to publicly advocate for the appointment of women to the STF as part of a strategy to regain female voters after criticism from his former stepdaughter, Michelle Bolsonaro. He intends to focus especially on the vacancy left by Minister Cármen Lúcia, the only woman currently on the court, and has already held a meeting with conservative women in Brasília.

item.title: EUA: Flávio e Figueiredo vão culpar Lula por acusações contra o Brasil
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and journalist Paulo Figueiredo will attend a USTR public hearing on July 6, blaming the Lula government and Brazil’s Supreme Court for U.S. allegations of unfair trade practices, including secret court orders to remove social media content, favoring Pix, insufficient anti-corruption enforcement, inadequate counterfeit enforcement, and disrupted ethanol tariff reciprocity, which could trigger a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods.

item.title: Michelle deixa comando do PL Mulher com saldo de 72 mil filiações
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro stepped down from leading PL Women after overseeing over 72,000 new female party affiliations between March 2023 and May 2026, contributing to a total of 397,000 women affiliated with the party by 2025. Under her leadership, the PL elected 1,005 women in the 2024 municipal elections, with 995 retaining office — including 61 mayors, such as Emilia Correia of Aracaju, one of only two women elected to lead Brazilian state capitals that year. Party officials credit her efforts in structuring women’s directories across all 26 states and the Federal District for the party’s gains in female representation.

item.title: Eleições: governo Lula entrega obras em 12 cidades antes de restrições
item.description: The Lula government is delivering simultaneous infrastructure projects in 12 cities across seven states before electoral restrictions ban inaugurations starting Saturday. The events include openings of federal institute campuses, health units, and Minha Casa, Minha Vida housing, with participation from ministers and Vice President Geraldo Alckmin. The initiative aims to highlight government achievements in education, health, and housing ahead of the official election campaign.

item.title: Flávio recorre (de novo) a Trump e levanta a bola para gol de Lula
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro requested the U.S. government delay tariffs on Brazilian exports until after the 2026 elections, arguing they would give Lula a political advantage. The move was criticized by Noblat as a tactical error that ended up benefiting the government, and Lula labeled the request as an act of treason against the nation.

item.title: Aliados do PL "abandonam" Michelle Bolsonaro após briga com Flávio
item.description: Allies of the PL abandoned Michelle Bolsonaro following her public feud with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, with only Senator Damares Alves expressing support. PL president Valdemar Costa Neto criticized her for sharing an unverified video by Anthony Garotinho about alleged parties involving Daniel Vorcaro, calling it a mistake. The conflict arose amid political maneuvering in Ceará, where Michelle opposes the PL’s alignment with Ciro Gomes, while Flávio seeks to limit the damage.

item.title: Flávio pede aos EUA pausa de 180 dias antes de novas tarifas
item.description: Senator and presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro requested the U.S. to delay the implementation of 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods by 180 days, proposing a 'snapback' mechanism that would automatically reinstate the tariffs if negotiations fail. The period could be extended by 90 additional days if talks show concrete progress and are conducted in good faith. The proposal aims to reduce electoral volatility and create a responsible space for bilateral trade negotiations between Brazil and the United States.

item.title: PGR revela sensatez ao pedir que Bolsonaro continue em domiciliar
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (PGR) urged the STF to maintain the house arrest of former President Jair Bolsonaro, arguing that the seizure of a pistol registered in his name does not constitute a disciplinary offense capable of worsening his penal situation. The statement was requested by Justice Alexandre de Moraes and reflects a stance of calm in a highly sensitive case, given Bolsonaro's 27-year-and-three-month sentence for attempted coup and other crimes.

item.title: Lula corre para entregar obras e chama lei eleitoral de 'papagaiada'
item.description: In Luís Gomes, Rio Grande do Norte, Lula inaugurated an irrigation tunnel without water, part of a rush to deliver projects before the legal electoral deadline. He criticized the current electoral law, calling it 'papagaiada' (parrot talk), implying it encourages empty promises and symbolic gestures. The article is subscriber-only and underscores the tension between public governance and electoral timing.

item.title: Pré-candidatos miram eleitoras e reforçam falas sobre mulheres em meio a polêmicas na pré-campanha
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates in 2026 intensified speeches targeting women, aiming to win over the female electorate, which represents 52.85% of Brazil's voters. The move follows controversies involving Michelle Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro, with the senator denying allegations of disrespect and framing women's issues as economic, not ideological.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz aos EUA que PIX não substitui cartão de crédito e sugere que meio de pagamento não seja conectado a sistemas 'não ocidentais'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) told U.S. officials that PIX does not replace credit cards and should not be linked to 'non-Western' payment systems, arguing that sanctions on PIX would harm U.S. investments. He requested a 180-day delay on 25% tariffs on Brazilian exports, stating that PIX is a sovereign public infrastructure and that conflict-of-interest claims are exaggerated, noting the Federal Reserve operates FedNow.

item.title: Ancelotti diz não ser 'nem gênio, nem tonto' e garante que Neymar já pode jogar por 90 minutos
item.description: Brazil's national team coach Carlo Ancelotti stated he is neither a genius nor a fool, following Brazil's victory over Japan in the 2026 World Cup. He praised the Brazilian people for their joy, unity, and humility, and confirmed that Neymar is physically capable of playing 90 minutes, though actual playing time will depend on match circumstances. Ancelotti also anticipated a tough match against Norway in the Round of 16, acknowledging Erling Haaland's quality while expressing confidence in his team's performance.

item.title: Lula incorpora chapéus ao visual e vira garoto-propaganda involuntário
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva began wearing hats regularly after undergoing skin cancer treatment in April 2024, turning the accessory into a notable part of his public image. What started as a health precaution has evolved into a symbol of his resilience and consistent presence in official appearances.

item.title: Kassab entra como vice de Caiado para ampliar poder de barganha do PSD no 2º turno, dizem aliados
item.description: The national president of the PSD, Gilberto Kassab, will run for vice president on Ronaldo Caiado's ticket to strengthen the party's bargaining power in a potential runoff of the 2026 election. The move aims to turn Caiado's candidacy from an individual project into a party initiative, as he recently joined the PSD.

item.title: Justiça nega pedido de deputado para concorrer à presidência do Crea-SP
item.description: The Federal Court in Brasília denied the request of state deputy Ricardo Madalena (PL) to run for president of Crea-SP, whose election takes place this Friday (3). The ruling blocks the legislator's candidacy, who sought to occupy the position in the São Paulo Regional Council of Engineering and Agronomy.

item.title: 'Lula é o único que quer o tarifaço', responde Flávio após presidente atribuir à família Bolsonaro nova taxa dos EUA
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) accused President Lula (PT) of being the only one interested in a new U.S. tariff on Brazilian products, claiming the government prioritized avoiding the classification of criminal factions as terrorists to benefit the PCC and Comando Vermelho. Lula had stated that Brazil 'is not for sale' and rejected Flávio's request to delay tariffs until after the 2026 elections, saying there is no justification for taxes on Brazilian exports. Flávio also said he personally defended PIX in meetings with Trump and Rubio, and plans to return to the U.S. to strengthen efforts against tariff imposition.

item.title: Novo líder da maioria na Câmara lista projetos prioritários e relata pedido de Lula
item.description: The new majority leader in the Chamber of Deputies, Silvio Costa Filho, stated his mission is to strengthen political articulation in Congress to help Lula’s government advance priority agendas by building consensus across right, left, and center. He highlighted priorities including fuel policy (focusing on ethanol and reducing operational costs), support for rural producers affected by extreme weather, and the creation of a national fund to combat femicide with potential for over R$10 billion in five years of investment. Costa Filho also emphasized that Lula asked him to act as a bridge between the Planalto and Congress, focusing on budget execution and voting on strategic projects.

item.title: Brasil e EUA: o novo capítulo das negociações sobre o tarifaço
item.description: The Brazilian government confirmed a new stage in negotiations with the United States to avoid tariffs on Brazilian products, following a meeting between Minister Márcio Elias Rosa and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. The dialogue was deemed constructive but requires more time to resolve differences, with expectations for a new ministerial meeting before July 15. Discussions cover six axes of the U.S. Section 301 investigation, including digital trade, ethanol, illegal deforestation, and intellectual property.

item.title: Fachin marca retomada de julgamento sobre a eleição no Rio de Janeiro para fim de agosto
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Edson Fachin has set August 26 for the resumption of the trial on the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election, after Minister Flávio Dino returned the case files and allowed plenary discussion. The debate centers on whether the election should be direct or indirect, with ministers divided: PSD advocates for direct election, while Fux, Mendonça, Marques, and Cármen Lúcia favored indirect election, some supporting secret ballot. Zanin backed direct election with open voting. The situation follows resignations and disqualifications of state officials, leading to the interim assumption of governance by the TJ-RJ president.

item.title: Nunes Marques faz balanço da preparação do TSE para as eleições de 2026
item.description: TSE President Minister Kassio Nunes Marques presented a progress report on preparations for the 2026 elections, highlighting advances in agreements with digital platforms to combat disinformation, 88 judgment sessions held, and 1,656 processes analyzed in the first half of the year. The TSE also launched the Voter's Manual in accessible language (being translated into indigenous languages) and the 'Your Vote Matters' program, providing free transportation for people with disabilities and remote communities, while strengthening coordination with regional electoral courts and expanding international electoral observation cooperation.

item.title: O grupo que mais criticou Michelle por seu vídeo sobre Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro gained over 100,000 followers after posting a video criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro, but lost approximately 10,200 followers from Monday to Thursday, according to Alek Maracajá, CEO of Ativa Web. 83% of the negative reactions came from men, suggesting a potential misogynistic backlash, although Michelle initially framed herself as a victim. PL president Valdemar Costa Neto suggested Michelle may withdraw from the Senate race and stop supporting Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign, despite her continued strong base among Christian and evangelical women.

item.title: Valdemar critica Flávio e Michelle por episódios envolvendo Vorcaro
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, criticized Michelle Bolsonaro for sharing an unreliable video from Anthony Garotinho about an alleged sex party involving Daniel Vorcaro, stating she 'did great harm' by spreading false information. He also reprimanded Flávio Bolsonaro for meeting with Vorcaro after his arrest, despite having initially sought him to finance the film 'Dark Horse' about Jair Bolsonaro, when Banco Master was not yet under accusation.

item.title: Nunes Marques marca reuniões com institutos de pesquisa e big techs
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques has scheduled meetings for July 14 and 16 with polling institutes and big tech companies to discuss electoral survey regulations and strategies to combat fake news. These meetings follow the suspension of an AtlasIntel poll showing a decline in Flávio Bolsonaro’s voter intent, which was challenged by the PL party over alleged methodological bias due to the inclusion of controversial audio involving the senator and a banker.

item.title: Aula de Haddad é interrompida por confusão com integrantes do MBL
item.description: The master class of PT's pre-candidate for São Paulo Governor, Fernando Haddad, was interrupted by a confrontation involving members of the Movimento Brasil Livre (MBL), who questioned him on issues such as the 'blusinhas tax' and his performance in the Education and Finance ministries. The disturbance included shoving, assaults, and interruptions to Haddad's speech, while he remained on stage throughout the incident. According to reports, the protesters were not Unicamp students and claimed they were assaulted during the confrontation.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro provoca Lula: "É o único que quer o tarifaço"
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro accused President Lula of being the only one pushing for a tariff hike on Brazilian products, claiming the president seeks to frame it as a false narrative of sovereignty defense to aid his re-election. Bolsonaro defended delaying the tariff, reiterated support for the Pix payment system, and said he would return to the U.S. to urge the Trump administration to avoid imposing a 25% tariff on Brazilian exports. Lula labeled the Bolsonaro family’s request as traitorous and against national interests.

item.title: Caso de mansão de R$ 10 mi ligada a Richarlison e Flávio volta a debate
item.description: The luxury mansion in Angra dos Reis, valued at R$10 million and linked to Richarlison, resurfaced in public debate after the footballer commented on Instagram that he lost the property and has not recovered his investment. Although Flávio Bolsonaro is not a party to the case, he was included as a witness after visiting the property with lawyer Willer Tomaz, a central figure in the dispute. In 2025, the STJ upheld a ruling favoring Tomaz’s possessory rights, denying Richarlison’s company’s appeal on grounds that it sought to re-examine evidence already reviewed by lower courts.

item.title: Cláudio Castro nega recebimento de dinheiro de bicheiro alvo da PF
item.description: The defense of former governor Cláudio Castro denied receiving any payment or illegal donation from bicheiro Adilson Oliveira Coutinho Filho, known as Adilsinho, stating that mere mention in a list does not prove wrongdoing. Castro emphasized that his 2022 campaign was regularly reported and approved by electoral justice, and that he is not a formal target of Operation Unha e Carne. He resigned as Rio governor in March 2026, one day before the TSE ruling on requests for his cassation and eight-year ineligibility.

item.title: Aula magna de Fernando Haddad na Unicamp tem confusão e briga; vídeo
item.description: Fernando Haddad's public lecture at Unicamp on Brazil's economic challenges was disrupted by protesters, leading to physical altercations. Security removed the demonstrators, and Haddad left the venue without speaking to the press. No injuries were reported.

item.title: Lula inaugura pilar de ponte e túnel de transposição sem água
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva inaugurated structural works in Bahia and Rio Grande do Norte, including a bridge pier and a water transfer tunnel, as part of an intensified travel agenda in the Northeast before the electoral deadline. The events were marked by public demands and technical setbacks, reflecting pressure to deliver visible results in an election year.

item.title: STF mantém suspensa votação que pode cassar o mandato de Renato Freitas no Paraná
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Luiz Edson Fachin upheld the suspension of a vote that could remove state deputy Renato Freitas (PT) from office, preserving an injunction from the Paraná Court of Justice that halted the ethics proceedings following a physical altercation in November 2025. The Paraná Legislative Assembly plans to bring the case before the full STF, arguing that the individual ministerial decision does not reflect the Court's position.

item.title: Lula acena a mulheres em meio a desgaste de Flávio com o eleitorado feminino
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva strengthened his appeal to female voters during a Northeastern agenda, advocating for increased penalties for femicide, electronic ankle bracelets for aggressors, and education as a path to women's independence. This move comes amid declining support for his main rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, among female voters following revelations of family turmoil involving Michelle Bolsonaro. Lula tied respect for women to family values and citizenship, framing gender-based violence prevention as a central pillar of his campaign.

item.title: À liberdade, portanto!
item.description: The author reflects on freedom as a value built through words, reflection, and overcoming internal and external obstacles. He criticizes the 6×1 work scale as unconstitutional because it prevents the constitutional right to leisure, suggesting it should be challenged in the STF via direct action of unconstitutionality. He also emphasizes the timely importance of dreams and memories as guides to correct past mistakes and live the present with greater awareness.

item.title: Governo não abre mão do PIX, mas apresenta novas medidas aos EUA para evitar tarifaço
item.description: The Lula government presented new measures to the U.S. in a meeting with Trade Representative Jamieson Greer to avoid a 25% additional tariff on Brazilian products, while maintaining its firm stance on PIX. The strategy aims to reinforce the 'status quo' of trade practices deemed non-unfair by Brazil, despite obstacles noted by Minister Marcio Elias Rosa. The deadline for a final decision is July 15, with another meeting scheduled before that date.

item.title: Governo Lula apresenta aos EUA plano de negociação para evitar tarifaço
item.description: The Lula government presented a negotiation plan to the U.S. to avoid a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, proposing tariff cuts on around 300 product lines, particularly in machinery and IT sectors, without harming domestic industry. Delivered by Minister Márcio Elias Rosa to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, the confidential document aims to address USTR concerns under WTO rules, while excluding topics like Pix and internal Brazilian politics.
